title: Add router markers and canonical semantics to Python and Rust configuration
description: Extend the Python and Rust status-definition models with router: boolean defaulting to false, and extend the canonical semantic categories to todo, in_progress, in_review, blocked, and done. Validate semantic-category values and router marker uniqueness with matching errors. When a router is enabled, require exactly one router-marked status for each canonical category. Remove router.workflow from both router configuration models and reject it as an unknown field. Preserve provider, class, WIP, retry, watch, forge, and coordination settings under the top-level router block. Acceptance: both runtimes load and validate the same YAML cases with parity-identical errors and parsed values.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Complete: merged in https://github.com/AnthusAI/Kanbus/pull/367 with CI green. Both runtimes: StatusDefinition has router: bool; canonical semantic categories are todo, in_progress, in_review, blocked and done, validated at load for every project; an enabled router needs exactly one router: true status per category; duplicate markers, missing markers, unsupported categories and unallowed lifecycle transitions fail with identical messages; router.workflow is rejected as an unknown field and the router's role lookups are derived from the markers (never read from or written to YAML), preserving provider, class, WIP, retry, watch, forge and coordination settings. Shared spec (kbs-b8f9e1) scenarios lost their @wip tag and pass in both runtimes. Verified by me: Rust cargo test --lib 542 passed and the full cucumber suite 1293 scenarios with 0 failed; Python full pytest clean and full behave 1400 scenarios with 0 failed. The repo .kanbus.yml is migrated with the markers reproducing the old roles (Ready is still the intake); kbs-38f428 flips intake to Discovery.
